region.text: Rarh (Radha), where the Senas served the Palas as sāmantas

ledger.note: 1070: Rarh is held under the Palas. 'The Senas entered into the service of Palas as sāmantas in Rāḍha, probably under Samantasena' (Sena page, undated; infobox 'Established: 1070', Samanta Sena 1070-1095); the Vijaya Sena page: Vijaya Sena 'inherited the position of a subordinate ruler in Rarh under the Palas'. So Rarh is a Pala-subordinate land until Hemanta Sena asserts kingship in 1095, not directly Sena land (added in the repair of 2026-10-19). Written from the subordinate's side as the review asked; pala-empire should carry the mirror, and its keyframes still draw Radha directly to 1161 (a mismatch for the Pala author).

1095: Hemanta Sena 'usurped power and styled himself king in 1095 AD' (Sena page); the Vijaya Sena page adds that Vijaya Sena 'obtained an independent position in Rarh in recognition of his help to Ramapala'. Rarh is Sena land in its own right from here.

region.text: southeastern Bengal (Vanga), ousted from the Varmans

ledger.note: c. 1152: Vijayasena ousts the Varmans from southeastern Bengal. 'So it seems probable that Vijaya Sena ousted the Varmans from southeastern Bengal in the middle of the 12th century AD' (Vijaya Sena page, no year). The Sena page has Vaṅga only 'by the end of' his reign (1159); the Barrackpur plate was 'issued from Vikrampur', the Varman capital. Dated 1152 (was c. 1150) to match the 1152 keyframe, which is the first to hold the land; the 1147 keyframe (Rarh only) covered 1147-1151.

1159: a part of Varendra. 'With the decline of the Pālas, their territory had expanded to include Vaṅga and a part of Varendra' by the end of Vijayasena's reign (1159); the Vijaya Sena page has Madanapala's authority in north Bengal run 'up to the 8th year of his reign, which falls in 1152-53' and his own supremacy in north and north-western Bengal after that. The Rajshahi division is the Pala dossier's reading of 'a part of Varendra'.

region.text: Gaur (Gauda) and the Bengal Delta outside the lands already Sena: Bengal without Rarh (Sena since 1070), southeastern Bengal (1152) and Rajshahi (the Varendra part, gained the same year)

ledger.note: 1159: Ballala Sena takes Gaur. 'Ballala Sena conquered Gaur from the Pala, became the ruler of the Bengal Delta, and made Nadia the capital as well' (Sena page; Ballala page: he 'ended the Pala Empire by defeating Govinda Pala'). Neither page dates the conquest; 1159 is the start of his reign on the Sena infobox (the Ballala page has 1160-1178). The Ballala page adds that he 'conquered Mithila while Vijaya Sena was still alive' (north Bihar, undated, not drawn: Karnat Mithila). Region corrected in the repair of 2026-10-19 (it covered all of Bengal, including Rarh, Vanga and Rajshahi). The Vijaya Sena page puts the north-Bengal conquest earlier: he 'established his own supremacy in North and North Western Bengal by ousting the Palas sometime after 1152-53 AD' and 'compelled the king of Gauda to flee'; the Sena page gives Gaur to Ballala and no year, so 1159 stays (confidence 1) and the two pages are left in disagreement.
1159: Ballala Sena 'made Nadia the capital as well': the court is at Nadia (Nabadwip) beside Vikramapura, which the Vijaya Sena page names ('He had capital in Vijayapuri and Vikramapura').

region.text: the Pala territory in Bihar, 'their entire territory annexed'

Cliopatria's Pala shape ends in 1168 (307 cells: Bihar 220, Jharkhand 85) and its Sena shape is recomposed in 1169. The year is a bridge from 'after 1165' to Cliopatria's 1169 (confidence 1). The 1169 keyframe now holds this land (repair of 2026-10-19; it used to be Bengal only, so keyframe and ledger disagreed). Counterpart: pala-empire dissolves in 1161 in its own dossier (infobox 'Disestablished 1161') and hands the same land to the Senas then, while the Sena page puts the annexation after 1165 and the Pala dossier's note has a Gaya line (Govindapala, Palapala) lasting to about 1200; the Ballala Sena page has Ballala 'ended the Pala Empire by defeating Govinda Pala'. The pages disagree on the year (1161 against after 1165); the counterpart stays pala-empire and the year is for the Pala author to agree.

notes:
WHAT THE ROW IS. Cliopatria's 'Sena Dynasty' row (1072-1235, 8 shapes) is one outline of 893-906 cells (about 254,000-258,000 km2: Bangladesh 423, West Bengal 265, Jharkhand 74, Meghalaya 73, Bihar 26, Assam 13, Tripura 13, Odisha 11) for the whole life; its Pala neighbour (Bihar, 125,000 km2 in 1072) has no cell in common with it. The Sena page has the family start as Pala sāmantas in Rarh in 1070, spread to Vanga and part of Varendra by 1159, take Gaur and the Pala territory under Ballala Sena and annex Bihar after 1165, then lose Nadia in 1203-1204 and survive in southeastern Bengal to about 1230. Cliopatria therefore draws the Bengal of c. 1170 for 1072-1158 (shapes 1072-1147 marked wrong, 1152 adjusted) and for 1204-1235 (1227 wrong). The Pala dossier raises the same point and keeps Radha and Varendra for the Palas, so Bengal is not drawn twice once both are corrected.

START/END. Cliopatria 1072-1235; the infobox gives 1070 (Samanta Sena 1070-1095) and 1230, and descendants 'till at least 1245 or 1260' (Tabaqat-i-Nasiri). Used 1070-1230; the 1231-1235 years are not drawn. Reign dates differ by a year between the pages (Vijaya Sena 1096-1159 or 1160; Ballala Sena 1159-1179 or 1160-1178; Lakshmana Sena 1179-1206 or 1178-1206): the infobox of the dynasty page is used.

DISAGREEMENTS AND SILENCES. (1) The year of Nadia: 'In 1203-1204 AD' in the text, 'Ghurid conquest of Bengal: 1205' in the infobox; the Bakhtiyar page gives Bihar 1200 and no year for Nadia (1204 used). (2) The Vijaya Sena page claims a rule 'over the whole of Bengal' by the middle of the 12th century, while the Sena page has Vanga and a part of Varendra only by 1159; the Vijaya page itself says Madanapala held north Bengal to 1152-53. The Sena page is used. (3) Mithila (Ballala Sena, 'while Vijaya Sena was still alive'), Kamarupa, Kalinga, Magadha and Kashi (Lakshmana Sena's 'peak') and Odisha 'possibly up to Varanasi' are undated and partly hedged on the pages; none is drawn. (4) Sena-Gahadavala conflicts 1155-1206 are an infobox line only: no contest events. (5) Hemanta Sena's 1095 assertion of kingship (end of Pala subordination) has no event type of its own; the Pala dossier would carry a vassal tint for 1070-1095 if it wanted one. (6) The Deva dynasty and the Khalji dynasty of Bengal are named only as successors in the infobox. (7) Rulers: the infobox list is used; Surya Sena, Narayana Sena and Laksmana Sena II are undated and omitted.

COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT DOSSIERS: varman-dynasty-of-east-bengal (the Pala dossier's placeholder), deva-dynasty, the Khalji state of Bengal (Bakhtiyar 1204-1206; Iwaz Khalji 1208-1227, independent from Delhi after 1212) and karnat-dynasty-of-mithila. Gazetteer names wanted: Rarh/Radha, Varendra, Vanga (as a region), Gauda/Gaur, Nabadwip (Nadia), Bikrampur, Lakhnauti, Mithila.

REPAIR OF 2026-10-19 (reviewer findings, pages re-read). (1) Bihar: the 1169 correction now holds the Pala 1168 shape (307 cells) with Bengal, and a new keyframe 1200-1203 drops it after Bakhtiyar's conquest of Bihar in 1200 (new loss event 1200, confidence 2, counterpart ghurid-dynasty). The counterpart of the 1169 gain stays pala-empire although its dossier dissolves in 1161; I cannot reconcile the infobox year (1161) with the Sena page's 'sometime after 1165' and left the year for the Pala author. (2) Rarh: vassal_start 1070 and vassal_end 1095 against pala-empire (confidence 2); pala-empire's keyframes must drop Radha from 1095. (3) South-eastern Bengal: the gain is dated 1152 to match the 1152 keyframe.
